column1: There are now over 700 million motor vehicles in the world – and the number is rising by more than 40 million each year.
column2: 目前全球机动车数量已超过7亿辆，且每年增长超过4000万辆。

column1: The average distance driven by car users is growing too – from 8 km a day per person in western Europe in 1965 to 25 km a day in 1995.
column2: 汽车用户的平均日行驶距离正在增长——从1965年西欧每人每天8公里，到1995年每天25公里。

column1: This dependence on motor vehicles has given rise to major problems, including environmental pollution, depletion of oil resources, traffic congestion and safety.
column2: 这种对机动车的依赖带来了许多问题，包括环境污染、石油资源枯竭、交通拥堵以及安全问题。

column1: While emissions from new cars are far less harmful than they used to be, city streets and motorways are becoming more crowded than ever, often with older trucks, buses and taxis, which emit excessive levels of smoke and fumes.
column2: 尽管新车的排放远不如以前有害，但城市街道和高速公路却越来越拥挤，常常充斥着老旧的卡车、公交车和出租车，这些车辆排放出过量的烟雾和废气。

column1: This concentration of vehicles makes air quality in urban areas unpleasant and sometimes dangerous to breathe.
column2: 这些车辆的大量聚集使得城市地区的空气质量令人不适，有时甚至会对人们的呼吸造成危害。

column1: Even Moscow has joined the list of capitals afflicted by congestion and traffic fumes.
column2: 就连莫斯科也加入了那些因交通拥堵和尾气污染而困扰的城市行列。

column1: In Mexico City, vehicle pollution is a major health hazard.
column2: 在墨西哥城，车辆排放造成的污染是一个严重的健康问题。

column1: Until a hundred years ago, most journeys were in the 20 km range, the distance conveniently accessible by horse.
column2: 直到一百年前，大多数旅行距离都在20公里以内，而这样的距离用马匹运输是相当方便的。

column1: Heavy freight could only be carried by water or rail.
column2: 重型货物只能通过水路或铁路运输。

column1: The invention of the motor vehicle brought personal mobility to the masses and made rapid freight delivery possible over a much wider area.
column2: 机动车的发明使大众获得了个人机动性，并使在更广泛的区域内实现快速货运成为可能。

column1: Today about 90 per cent of inland freight in the United Kingdom is carried by road.
column2: 如今，在英国，大约90%的内陆货运由公路运输完成。

column1: Clearly, the world cannot revert to the horse-drawn wagon.
column2: 显然，世界无法再回到马车时代。

column1: Can it avoid being locked into congested and polluting ways of transporting people and goods?
column2: 它能否避免被锁定在拥堵且污染严重的运输方式中？

column1: In Europe, most cities are still designed for the old modes of transport.
column2: 在欧洲，大多数城市仍以传统的交通方式为规划和建设的基础。

column1: Adaptation to the motor car has involved adding ring roads, one-way systems and parking lots.
column2: 对汽车的适应包括修建环形道路、实施单向交通系统以及设置停车场。

column1: In the United States, more land is assigned to car use than to housing.
column2: 在美国，用于汽车使用的土地比用于住房的土地还要多。

column1: Urban sprawl means that life without a car is next to impossible.
column2: 城市蔓延意味着没有汽车的生活几乎是不可能的。

column1: Mass use of motor vehicles has also killed or injured millions of people.
column2: 机动车的广泛使用也导致了数以百万计的人死亡或受伤。

column1: Other social effects have been blamed on the car such as alienation and aggressive human behaviour.
column2: 有人将汽车归咎于社会疏离和攻击性的人类行为。

column1: A 1993 study by the European Federation for Transport and Environment found that car transport is seven times as costly as rail travel in terms of the external social costs it entails such as congestion, accidents, pollution, loss of cropland and natural habitats, depletion of oil resources, and so on.
column2: 欧洲交通与环境联合会在1993年进行的一项研究指出，从外部社会成本的角度来看，汽车运输的成本是铁路运输的七倍。这些成本包括交通拥堵、交通事故、污染问题、农田和自然栖息地的丧失、石油资源的枯竭等。

column1: Yet cars easily surpass trains or buses as a flexible and convenient mode of personal transport.
column2: 不过，汽车作为一种灵活且便捷的个人交通工具，显然优于火车或公交车。

column1: It is unrealistic to expect people to give up private cars in favour of mass transit.
column2: 人们指望放弃私家车转而使用公共交通是不切实际的。

column1: Technical solutions can reduce the pollution problem and increase the fuel efficiency of engines.
column2: 技术解决方案能够有效减少污染问题，并提高发动机的燃油效率。

column1: But fuel consumption and exhaust emissions depend on which cars are preferred by customers and how they are driven.
column2: 汽车的燃油消耗和尾气排放实际上取决于客户更倾向于使用哪种车型，以及驾驶方式如何。

column1: Many people buy larger cars than they need for daily purposes or waste fuel by driving aggressively.
column2: 许多人购买的汽车比日常所需更大，或因驾驶急躁而浪费燃料。

column1: Besides, global car use is increasing at a faster rate than the improvement in emissions and fuel efficiency which technology is now making possible.
column2: 此外，全球汽车使用量的增长速度，已快于技术所能实现的排放和燃油效率改善程度。

column1: One solution that has been put forward is the long-term solution of designing cities and neighbourhoods so that car journeys are not necessary – all essential services being located within walking distance or easily accessible by public transport.
column2: 一种被提出的方法是，从长远角度设计城市和社区，使驾车出行不再必要——所有基本服务都位于步行范围内或可通过公共交通轻松抵达。

column1: Not only would this save energy and cut carbon dioxide emissions, it would also enhance the quality of community life, putting the emphasis on people instead of cars.
column2: 这不仅会节约能源、减少二氧化碳排放，还将提升社区生活质量，把重点放在人而不是汽车上。

column1: Good local government is already bringing this about in some places.
column2: 在一些地方，良好的地方政府管理已经实现了这一目标。

column1: But few democratic communities are blessed with the vision – and the capital – to make such profound changes in modern lifestyles.
column2: 但是，很少有民主社会能够拥有这样的远见——以及足够的资源来推动现代生活方式的深刻变革。

column1: A more likely scenario seems to be a combination of mass transit systems for travel into and around cities, with small ‘low emission’ cars for urban use and larger hybrid or lean burn cars for use elsewhere.
column2: 更可能的情景是，结合使用公共交通系统来往返城市各处，同时利用小型、低排放汽车进行城市内的出行，而大型混合动力车或节能型汽车则用于其他地区的出行需求。

column1: Electronically tolled highways might be used to ensure that drivers pay charges geared to actual road use.
column2: 电子收费高速公路可以用来确保驾驶员支付与实际道路使用量相对应的费用。

column1: Better integration of transport systems is also highly desirable – and made more feasible by modern computers.
column2: 更完善的交通系统整合也是非常必要的——而现代计算机技术的出现使得这一目标变得更加可行。

column1: But these are solutions for countries which can afford them.
column2: 但这些方案仅适用于那些能够负担得起的国家。

column1: In most developing countries, old cars and old technologies continue to predominate.
column2: 在大多数发展中国家，老旧汽车和落后技术仍然占据主导地位。
